page: Amazon Web Services r7g.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized compute offering powered by custom AWS Graviton processor silicon. It provides dedicated access to 64 physical cores built on the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 microarchitecture operating at 2.6 GHz, running one thread per core without hyper-threading. The hardware configuration couples these dedicated Arm cores with 512.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory (8.0 GB per physical core) and provides a 30 Gbps baseline network throughput. No local SSD storage is bundled with the bare-metal host, requiring persistent storage to be attached over the network, and the configuration contains zero GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant multi-core throughput alongside high memory efficiency. The platform achieves top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core performance (21,125.0) and software compilation using Clang (60,717.0), as well as a top-tier PassMark memory score (3,189.13). Multi-core compute strength is further reinforced by a strong stress-ng multi-core score (98,068.21) and sustained memory read bandwidth reaching 253.87 GB/sec on large uncached blocks. Single-thread processing remains within average ranges across Geekbench (1,551.0) and stress-ng (1,536.08), highlighting an architecture designed to deliver aggregate multi-threaded execution rather than peak single-core clock velocity.

The 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio, high-bandwidth DDR5 subsystem, and non-virtualized bare-metal execution make r7g.metal an efficient platform for resource-dense memory workloads. While software stacks require ARM64 compilation and lack x86-specific instruction sets like AVX, workloads with broad multi-core concurrency benefit from strong throughput density. The system excels in large-scale in-memory databases such as Redis (recording 103.78 million SET operations per second), relational database operations, high-throughput static web serving, and intensive CI/CD compilation pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r7g.metal is a bare-metal memory-optimized instance featuring 64 dedicated physical cores on the 64-bit AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 ARMv8 architecture running at 2.6 GHz. Operating without hypervisor overhead or hyper-threading, the server pairs its 64 cores with 512.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory, achieving an 8.0 GB-per-core ratio, alongside 30 Gbps baseline networking. It includes no internal local storage and no GPU hardware. Synthetic benchmarks highlight exceptional aggregate performance, including top-tier Geekbench multi-core and PassMark memory bandwidth measurements, paired with strong throughput in Redis SET operations and Clang compilations. Single-core processing metrics remain balanced within median percentiles. This dense memory footprint and high parallel throughput profile make r7g.metal well aligned for in-memory caches, distributed databases, large-scale software build environments, and enterprise data processing systems adapted for ARM64 environments.
